ps.e: Most animals do their best to avoid the cold.
ps.b: বেশিরভাগ প্রাণী ঠান্ডা এড়িয়ে চলতে সর্বোচ্চ চেষ্টা করে।

ps.e: Emperor penguins do the opposite.
ps.b: সম্রাট পেঙ্গুইন করে ঠিক উল্টোটা।

ps.e: They are the only birds that spend the whole Antarctic winter on the ice, where the temperature can fall far below minus forty degrees Celsius and the wind can blow at the speed of a train.
ps.b: এরা একমাত্র পাখি যারা পুরো অ্যান্টার্কটিক শীত বরফের ওপর কাটায়, যেখানে তাপমাত্রা মাইনাস চল্লিশ ডিগ্রি সেলসিয়াসের অনেক নিচে নামতে পারে আর বাতাস ট্রেনের গতিতে বইতে পারে।

ps.e: And that is exactly the time of year when they choose to raise their young.
ps.b: আর ঠিক বছরের সেই সময়টাতেই তারা বাচ্চা বড় করার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়।

ps.e: The story begins in autumn, when thousands of emperor penguins walk many kilometres inland from the sea to the breeding place, which is called a colony.
ps.b: গল্পটি শুরু হয় হেমন্তে, যখন হাজার হাজার সম্রাট পেঙ্গুইন সমুদ্র থেকে অনেক কিলোমিটার ভেতরে প্রজননস্থলে হেঁটে যায়, যাকে বলা হয় কলোনি।

ps.e: Each pair of penguins meets and, in May or June, the female lays a single egg.
ps.b: প্রতিটি জোড়া পেঙ্গুইন মিলিত হয় এবং মে বা জুন মাসে স্ত্রী পেঙ্গুইনটি একটি মাত্র ডিম পাড়ে।

ps.e: Then something unusual happens.
ps.b: তারপর একটি অস্বাভাবিক ঘটনা ঘটে।

ps.e: She passes the egg carefully to her partner, and she walks back to the sea to feed, because laying the egg has used up much of her strength.
ps.b: সে সাবধানে ডিমটি তার সঙ্গীর কাছে হস্তান্তর করে এবং খাবার খেতে সমুদ্রে ফিরে যায়, কারণ ডিম পাড়তে গিয়ে তার অনেক শক্তি খরচ হয়ে গেছে।

ps.e: The male now takes over.
ps.b: এবার পুরুষ পেঙ্গুইন দায়িত্ব নেয়।

ps.e: He balances the egg on top of his feet and covers it with a warm flap of skin, called a brood pouch, so that it never touches the ice.
ps.b: সে ডিমটি পায়ের ওপর ভারসাম্য করে রাখে এবং ব্রুড পাউচ নামের উষ্ণ চামড়ার ভাঁজ দিয়ে ঢেকে দেয়, যাতে তা কখনও বরফ স্পর্শ না করে।

ps.e: If the egg touched the ice, it would freeze within minutes.
ps.b: ডিম বরফ ছুঁলে কয়েক মিনিটেই জমে যেত।

ps.e: For about two months, through the worst weather on Earth, the male stands almost without moving, and during all this time he does not eat.
ps.b: প্রায় দুই মাস ধরে, পৃথিবীর সবচেয়ে খারাপ আবহাওয়ার মধ্যে পুরুষটি প্রায় নড়াচড়া না করে দাঁড়িয়ে থাকে, আর এই পুরো সময় সে কিছু খায় না।

ps.e: To survive, the males work together.
ps.b: টিকে থাকতে পুরুষরা একসঙ্গে কাজ করে।

ps.e: They gather into a huddle, standing close to each other with their bodies touching.
ps.b: তারা একটি জটলা পাকায়, একে অপরের গা ঘেঁষে দাঁড়ায়।

ps.e: Penguins on the windy outer edge slowly move to the inside, while those in the middle take their turn on the outside.
ps.b: বাতাসের দিকে থাকা বাইরের কিনারার পেঙ্গুইনরা ধীরে ধীরে ভেতরে সরে যায়, আর মাঝখানের পেঙ্গুইনরা পালা করে বাইরে আসে।

ps.e: In this way no penguin has to suffer the worst cold for long.
ps.b: এভাবে কোনো পেঙ্গুইনকে বেশিক্ষণ সবচেয়ে তীব্র ঠান্ডা সইতে হয় না।

ps.e: The huddle can make the temperature in the middle surprisingly warm.
ps.b: এই জটলা মাঝখানের তাপমাত্রাকে আশ্চর্যজনকভাবে উষ্ণ করে তুলতে পারে।

ps.e: By the time the chick hatches, the male has lost a large part of his body weight.
ps.b: ছানা ডিম ফুটে বের হওয়ার সময় পুরুষটি তার শরীরের ওজনের একটি বড় অংশ হারিয়ে ফেলেছে।

ps.e: At this moment the females return from the sea, with their stomachs full of food.
ps.b: ঠিক তখন স্ত্রী পেঙ্গুইনরা সমুদ্র থেকে পেট ভর্তি খাবার নিয়ে ফিরে আসে।

ps.e: A female recognises her partner by his call, and she feeds the chick.
ps.b: স্ত্রী তার সঙ্গীকে তার ডাক শুনে চিনতে পারে এবং ছানাকে খাওয়ায়।

ps.e: Now it is the male's turn to go and eat, and for the next few months the parents take turns to look after their chick.
ps.b: এবার পুরুষের পালা খেতে যাওয়ার, আর পরের কয়েক মাস বাবা-মা পালা করে ছানার দেখাশোনা করে।

ps.e: When the chick has grown enough to keep warm, both parents spend more time at the sea, and the chicks gather in groups.
ps.b: ছানা যখন নিজে উষ্ণ থাকার মতো বড় হয়, দুজন বাবা-মা-ই সমুদ্রে বেশি সময় কাটায়, আর ছানারা দল বেঁধে থাকে।

ps.e: They remain on the sea ice until their waterproof feathers grow, which happens in the summer, when the ice starts to break up.
ps.b: তারা সমুদ্রের বরফের ওপর থাকে যতক্ষণ না তাদের পানিরোধী পালক গজায়, যা ঘটে গ্রীষ্মে, যখন বরফ ভাঙতে শুরু করে।

ps.e: The timing is very important.
ps.b: সময়টা খুব গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।

ps.e: If the ice breaks too soon, the chicks may fall into the water before their feathers are ready.
ps.b: বরফ খুব তাড়াতাড়ি ভাঙলে ছানারা পালক তৈরি হওয়ার আগেই পানিতে পড়ে যেতে পারে।

ps.e: This is exactly what worries scientists.
ps.b: ঠিক এটাই বিজ্ঞানীদের উদ্বিগ্ন করছে।

ps.e: Emperor penguins depend on stable sea ice.
ps.b: সম্রাট পেঙ্গুইন স্থিতিশীল সমুদ্রের বরফের ওপর নির্ভর করে।

ps.e: In 2022, satellite pictures showed that in one region of Antarctica the ice broke up early, and almost all of the chicks in several colonies were probably lost.
ps.b: ২০২২ সালে স্যাটেলাইট ছবিতে দেখা গেল, অ্যান্টার্কটিকার একটি অঞ্চলে বরফ আগেভাগে ভেঙে গিয়েছিল, আর বেশ কয়েকটি কলোনির প্রায় সব ছানাই সম্ভবত মারা গিয়েছিল।

ps.e: As the world becomes warmer, the sea ice may become less reliable, and emperor penguin numbers could fall.
ps.b: বিশ্ব আরও উষ্ণ হলে সমুদ্রের বরফ কম নির্ভরযোগ্য হতে পারে, আর সম্রাট পেঙ্গুইনের সংখ্যা কমে যেতে পারে।

ps.e: The emperor penguin is a creature of great patience and teamwork.
ps.b: সম্রাট পেঙ্গুইন প্রবল ধৈর্য ও দলগত কাজের এক প্রাণী।

ps.e: Its way of life shows how animals can adapt to the hardest conditions on Earth, and it reminds us that even the toughest species can be harmed when the world around them changes.
ps.b: এর জীবনযাপন দেখায় কীভাবে প্রাণীরা পৃথিবীর কঠিনতম পরিস্থিতিতেও খাপ খাইয়ে নিতে পারে, আর এটি মনে করিয়ে দেয়, সবচেয়ে শক্ত প্রজাতিও ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হতে পারে যখন তাদের চারপাশের পৃথিবী বদলে যায়।

cmp/24.sub: The revival of the Welsh language
cmp/24.title: A Language That Refused to Disappear
cmp/24.src: Welsh Government; Office for National Statistics; National Library of Wales; BBC History
p: There are about seven thousand languages in the world, and experts believe that roughly one language disappears every few months. The pattern is usually the same. A small language is surrounded by a large and powerful one, parents decide that the large language will give their children better chances, and within a few generations the old tongue is spoken only by the elderly. Wales, a small country in the west of Great Britain, looked as if it was heading the same way. Yet its language, Welsh, has done something unusual: it has survived, and in some respects it has grown stronger.

The decline was dramatic. In 1911, around forty-four percent of people in Wales spoke Welsh. By the early 1980s, the figure had fallen to about nineteen percent. Several forces were responsible. Industrial work drew families to towns where English was the language of employment, and English dominated the schools, the courts and the newspapers. In nineteenth-century classrooms, some children who were heard speaking Welsh were made to wear a wooden board, known as the "Welsh Not", around their necks. The aim was to teach children that their language was a disadvantage.

The turning point came when people stopped treating the language as a private habit and began to see it as a matter of public life. Campaigners, including students who painted over English road signs, argued that Welsh should have the same standing as English. Their protests were not always popular, and some campaigners went to prison. Gradually, however, politicians listened. The Welsh Language Act of 1993 required public bodies to treat Welsh and English equally, and later laws strengthened this position.

Education proved to be the most powerful tool. Welsh-language schools, which teach most lessons in Welsh, first opened in the 1930s and 1940s, and they have expanded steadily since. Children from English-speaking homes often attend them, and most become fluent. Every pupil in Wales now learns Welsh up to the age of sixteen. In effect, the schools have turned a language that families had stopped passing on into one that children can learn in the classroom.

The media has helped as well. A Welsh-language television channel, S4C, began broadcasting in 1982, and Welsh radio, music and online content have followed. Seeing the language on screens and hearing it in popular songs has changed its image. Welsh is no longer associated only with chapels and farms; it is also the language of comedy, football commentary and young people's social media. Even free language apps now offer Welsh lessons.

The results, however, are mixed. The 2021 census showed that about 17.8 percent of people aged three and over could speak Welsh, which is a little lower than ten years earlier, despite the investment in schools. One explanation is that many children learn Welsh at school but do not use it at home or with friends, so the skill fades. Another is that the older generation of native speakers is shrinking. Learning a language, as many people discover, is not the same as living in it.

The Welsh Government has set a bold target: one million Welsh speakers by 2050, which would be roughly a third of the population. Critics argue that the target is unrealistic unless more adults are given the chance to learn and unless Welsh becomes the normal language of workplaces and communities, not just classrooms. Supporters reply that setting a high goal is the only way to create the necessary effort.

Whatever the final result, the Welsh story offers lessons for other small languages. A language does not survive by sentiment alone. It needs the support of laws, schools, media and, above all, ordinary speakers who choose to use it every day. Wales has shown that decline is not inevitable, but it has also shown how much work is required to reverse it.

ps.b: ওয়েলস, গ্রেট ব্রিটেনের পশ্চিমে অবস্থিত একটি ছোট দেশ, দেখে মনে হচ্ছিল একই পথে যাচ্ছে।

ps.e: Yet its language, Welsh, has done something unusual: it has survived, and in some respects it has grown stronger.
ps.b: তবু এর ভাষা, ওয়েলশ, অস্বাভাবিক কিছু করেছে: এটি টিকে আছে, আর কিছু দিক থেকে আরও শক্তিশালীও হয়েছে।

ps.e: The decline was dramatic.
ps.b: পতনটি ছিল নাটকীয়।

ps.e: In 1911, around forty-four percent of people in Wales spoke Welsh.
ps.b: ১৯১১ সালে ওয়েলসের প্রায় চুয়াল্লিশ শতাংশ মানুষ ওয়েলশ বলত।

ps.e: By the early 1980s, the figure had fallen to about nineteen percent.
ps.b: ১৯৮০-র দশকের শুরুতে এই সংখ্যা নেমে আসে প্রায় উনিশ শতাংশে।

ps.e: Several forces were responsible.
ps.b: এর পেছনে ছিল বেশ কয়েকটি কারণ।

ps.e: Industrial work drew families to towns where English was the language of employment, and English dominated the schools, the courts and the newspapers.
ps.b: শিল্পের কাজ পরিবারগুলোকে টেনে নিয়ে গেল এমন শহরে যেখানে ইংরেজিই ছিল চাকরির ভাষা, আর স্কুল, আদালত ও সংবাদপত্রে ইংরেজির আধিপত্য ছিল।

ps.e: In nineteenth-century classrooms, some children who were heard speaking Welsh were made to wear a wooden board, known as the "Welsh Not", around their necks.
ps.b: উনবিংশ শতাব্দীর শ্রেণিকক্ষে যেসব শিশুকে ওয়েলশ বলতে শোনা যেত, তাদের কারও কারও গলায় কাঠের একটি ফলক ঝুলিয়ে দেওয়া হতো, যা "ওয়েলশ নট" নামে পরিচিত।

ps.e: The aim was to teach children that their language was a disadvantage.
ps.b: উদ্দেশ্য ছিল শিশুদের শেখানো যে তাদের ভাষা একটি অসুবিধা।

ps.e: The turning point came when people stopped treating the language as a private habit and began to see it as a matter of public life.
ps.b: মোড় ঘুরল তখন, যখন মানুষ ভাষাটিকে ব্যক্তিগত অভ্যাস হিসেবে দেখা বন্ধ করে একে জনজীবনের একটি বিষয় হিসেবে দেখতে শুরু করল।

ps.e: Campaigners, including students who painted over English road signs, argued that Welsh should have the same standing as English.
ps.b: প্রচারকারীরা, যাদের মধ্যে ছিল ইংরেজি রাস্তার সাইনবোর্ডে রং লেপে দেওয়া শিক্ষার্থীরাও, যুক্তি দিল যে ওয়েলশের ইংরেজির মতোই মর্যাদা পাওয়া উচিত।

ps.e: Their protests were not always popular, and some campaigners went to prison.
ps.b: তাদের প্রতিবাদ সবসময় জনপ্রিয় ছিল না, আর কিছু প্রচারকারী কারাগারেও গেছেন।

ps.e: Gradually, however, politicians listened.
ps.b: তবে ধীরে ধীরে রাজনীতিবিদরা কথা শুনলেন।

ps.e: The Welsh Language Act of 1993 required public bodies to treat Welsh and English equally, and later laws strengthened this position.
ps.b: ১৯৯৩ সালের ওয়েলশ ভাষা আইন সরকারি সংস্থাগুলোকে ওয়েলশ ও ইংরেজিকে সমানভাবে দেখতে বাধ্য করল, আর পরবর্তী আইনগুলো এই অবস্থানকে আরও শক্ত করল।

ps.e: Education proved to be the most powerful tool.
ps.b: শিক্ষা প্রমাণিত হলো সবচেয়ে শক্তিশালী হাতিয়ার।

ps.e: Welsh-language schools, which teach most lessons in Welsh, first opened in the 1930s and 1940s, and they have expanded steadily since.
ps.b: ওয়েলশ-ভাষার স্কুল, যেখানে বেশিরভাগ পাঠ ওয়েলশে পড়ানো হয়, প্রথম চালু হয় ১৯৩০ ও ১৯৪০-এর দশকে, আর তখন থেকে স্থিরভাবে বিস্তৃত হয়েছে।

ps.e: Children from English-speaking homes often attend them, and most become fluent.
ps.b: ইংরেজিভাষী ঘরের শিশুরাও প্রায়ই এসব স্কুলে পড়ে, আর বেশিরভাগই সাবলীল হয়ে ওঠে।

ps.e: Every pupil in Wales now learns Welsh up to the age of sixteen.
ps.b: ওয়েলসের প্রতিটি শিক্ষার্থী এখন ষোল বছর বয়স পর্যন্ত ওয়েলশ শেখে।

ps.e: In effect, the schools have turned a language that families had stopped passing on into one that children can learn in the classroom.
ps.b: বাস্তবে স্কুলগুলো এমন একটি ভাষাকে, যা পরিবারগুলো পরবর্তী প্রজন্মকে দেওয়া বন্ধ করে দিয়েছিল, শিশুরা শ্রেণিকক্ষে শিখতে পারে এমন ভাষায় পরিণত করেছে।

ps.e: The media has helped as well.
ps.b: গণমাধ্যমও সাহায্য করেছে।

ps.e: A Welsh-language television channel, S4C, began broadcasting in 1982, and Welsh radio, music and online content have followed.
ps.b: ওয়েলশ-ভাষার একটি টেলিভিশন চ্যানেল, এস৪সি, ১৯৮২ সালে সম্প্রচার শুরু করে, আর এরপর এসেছে ওয়েলশ রেডিও, গান ও অনলাইন কনটেন্ট।

ps.e: Seeing the language on screens and hearing it in popular songs has changed its image.
ps.b: পর্দায় ভাষাটিকে দেখা এবং জনপ্রিয় গানে শোনা এর ভাবমূর্তি বদলে দিয়েছে।

ps.e: Welsh is no longer associated only with chapels and farms; it is also the language of comedy, football commentary and young people's social media.
ps.b: ওয়েলশ এখন আর কেবল ছোট গির্জা ও খামারের সঙ্গে যুক্ত নয়; এটি কৌতুক, ফুটবল ধারাভাষ্য ও তরুণদের সামাজিক মাধ্যমেরও ভাষা।

ps.e: Even free language apps now offer Welsh lessons.
ps.b: এমনকি বিনামূল্যের ভাষা-শিক্ষার অ্যাপেও এখন ওয়েলশ পাঠ আছে।

ps.e: The results, however, are mixed.
ps.b: ফলাফল অবশ্য মিশ্র।

ps.e: The 2021 census showed that about 17.8 percent of people aged three and over could speak Welsh, which is a little lower than ten years earlier, despite the investment in schools.
ps.b: ২০২১ সালের আদমশুমারিতে দেখা গেল, তিন বছর ও তার বেশি বয়সী প্রায় ১৭.৮ শতাংশ মানুষ ওয়েলশ বলতে পারে, যা দশ বছর আগের চেয়ে কিছুটা কম, স্কুলে বিনিয়োগ সত্ত্বেও।

ps.e: One explanation is that many children learn Welsh at school but do not use it at home or with friends, so the skill fades.
ps.b: একটি ব্যাখ্যা হলো, অনেক শিশু স্কুলে ওয়েলশ শেখে কিন্তু ঘরে বা বন্ধুদের সঙ্গে ব্যবহার করে না, ফলে দক্ষতা ম্লান হয়ে যায়।

ps.e: Another is that the older generation of native speakers is shrinking.
ps.b: আরেকটি ব্যাখ্যা হলো, মাতৃভাষী প্রবীণ প্রজন্ম সংখ্যায় কমে আসছে।

ps.e: Learning a language, as many people discover, is not the same as living in it.
ps.b: অনেকে যেমন আবিষ্কার করেন, একটি ভাষা শেখা আর সেই ভাষায় জীবনযাপন করা এক নয়।

ps.e: The Welsh Government has set a bold target: one million Welsh speakers by 2050, which would be roughly a third of the population.
ps.b: ওয়েলশ সরকার একটি উচ্চাভিলাষী লক্ষ্য ঠিক করেছে: ২০৫০ সালের মধ্যে দশ লক্ষ ওয়েলশভাষী, যা জনসংখ্যার প্রায় এক-তৃতীয়াংশ হবে।

ps.e: Critics argue that the target is unrealistic unless more adults are given the chance to learn and unless Welsh becomes the normal language of workplaces and communities, not just classrooms.
ps.b: সমালোচকরা বলেন, লক্ষ্যটি অবাস্তব, যদি না আরও প্রাপ্তবয়স্ককে শেখার সুযোগ দেওয়া হয় এবং ওয়েলশ কেবল শ্রেণিকক্ষে নয়, কর্মক্ষেত্র ও সম্প্রদায়ের স্বাভাবিক ভাষা হয়ে ওঠে।

ps.e: Supporters reply that setting a high goal is the only way to create the necessary effort.
ps.b: সমর্থকরা জবাব দেন, উঁচু লক্ষ্য ঠিক করাই প্রয়োজনীয় প্রচেষ্টা তৈরির একমাত্র উপায়।

ps.e: Whatever the final result, the Welsh story offers lessons for other small languages.
ps.b: চূড়ান্ত ফল যাই হোক, ওয়েলশের গল্প অন্যান্য ছোট ভাষার জন্য শিক্ষা দেয়।

ps.e: A language does not survive by sentiment alone.
ps.b: একটি ভাষা কেবল আবেগের জোরে টিকে থাকে না।

ps.e: It needs the support of laws, schools, media and, above all, ordinary speakers who choose to use it every day.
ps.b: এর দরকার আইন, স্কুল, গণমাধ্যমের সমর্থন, আর সবার ওপরে সাধারণ ভাষাভাষীদের, যারা প্রতিদিন এটি ব্যবহার করবে বলে বেছে নেয়।

ps.e: Wales has shown that decline is not inevitable, but it has also shown how much work is required to reverse it.
ps.b: ওয়েলস দেখিয়েছে পতন অনিবার্য নয়, কিন্তু সেটি উল্টে দিতে কতটা পরিশ্রম লাগে তাও দেখিয়েছে।

cmp/25.title: The Encyclopedia Anyone Can Edit
p: When Wikipedia was launched in January 2001, many people laughed at the idea. An encyclopedia that anyone in the world could edit, without a degree, a salary or an editor-in-chief? It sounded like a recipe for chaos. Yet more than twenty years later, Wikipedia is one of the most visited websites on Earth, with millions of articles in English alone and versions in over three hundred languages. How has it survived?

The first part of the answer is people. Wikipedia is written and maintained by volunteers, most of whom are unpaid. They are supported by a non-profit organisation, the Wikimedia Foundation, which pays for servers and legal protection but does not decide what the articles say. Because anyone may correct a mistake, a large crowd of readers works as a very large team of proof-readers.

The second part is rules. Wikipedia has a small number of core principles that every editor is expected to follow. Articles must be written from a neutral point of view, which means that they should describe the main viewpoints fairly rather than argue for one. They must not contain "original research", so editors cannot publish their own theories. And most importantly, claims must be verifiable: a reader should be able to check them in a reliable published source, such as a book, a journal or a respected newspaper. This is why a well-edited article is full of numbered notes.

The third part is visibility. Every change made to an article is recorded, and anyone can look at the page history to see who changed what and when. Each article also has a talk page where editors discuss disagreements. If someone adds nonsense, other editors can undo the change within minutes, and sometimes within seconds, with the help of automatic programs that detect obvious vandalism. Articles on controversial subjects can be "protected", so that only experienced editors are allowed to change them.

But how accurate is Wikipedia? In 2005, the journal Nature asked experts to compare forty-two scientific entries from Wikipedia with the same entries in the Encyclopaedia Britannica. The reviewers found that the two were close in accuracy: the experts found an average of four mistakes in a Wikipedia article and three in a Britannica article. Britannica disputed the study, and the encyclopedias have changed greatly since then, but the result surprised many people.

This does not mean that Wikipedia is perfect. Its coverage is uneven. Subjects that interest its typical editors, such as computing, popular music and science fiction, are covered in great depth, while others receive far less attention. Surveys suggest that only a small minority of its editors are women, and that a much smaller share of its biographies are about women than about men. Information about places and cultures outside Europe and North America can also be thin. These gaps reflect the interests of the people who volunteer, not a deliberate plan.

There is a further problem: readers cannot always tell the difference between a well-checked article and one that has hardly been reviewed. A page about a popular topic may have been examined by hundreds of editors, while a page about a small village may have been written by one person years ago. Researchers therefore advise treating Wikipedia as a starting point rather than a final authority.

Teachers often tell students not to cite Wikipedia in their essays, and the advice is sensible. But many teachers also admit that it is a good place to begin. The most valuable habit is to follow the links at the bottom of the page and read the original sources. Used in this way, Wikipedia shows what its founders hoped: that millions of strangers, working by shared rules, can build something useful. It also shows that no source, however popular, should be believed without being questioned.

q.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
q.e: The passage explains the reasons for Wikipedia's success, its accuracy and its limits.
o: A. To tell readers not to use the internet
B. To describe the history of encyclopedias
C. To prove that Wikipedia is better than Britannica
D. To explain how Wikipedia works and how reliable it is

q.q: Wikipedia was launched in 2001.
Most of the people who write Wikipedia are paid by the Wikimedia Foundation.
q.e: Paragraph 2 says it is written by volunteers, most of whom are unpaid.

q.q: Which sentence best sums up paragraph 3?
q.e: Paragraph 3 explains neutrality, no original research and verifiability.
o: A. Wikipedia depends on a few core rules, especially that claims must be verifiable
B. Only experts with degrees can write articles on the site.
C. Wikipedia has no rules, and anyone can write anything.
D. Editors can publish their own theories if they are confident that they are right and have enough support.

q.q: What does "verifiable" mean in paragraph 3?
q.e: The paragraph explains that a reader should be able to check claims in a reliable source.
o: A. Claims can be checked in a reliable published source
B. Claims must be very long
C. Claims must come from the editor's own research
D. Claims must be new

q.q: What can other editors do if someone adds nonsense to an article?
q.e: Paragraph 4 says changes can be undone within minutes or seconds.
o: A. Delete the whole article
B. Send a letter to the editor
C. Wait for the Wikimedia Foundation to act
D. Undo the change, sometimes within seconds

q.q: A page history shows who has made changes to an article and when.
q.e: Paragraph 4 says every change is recorded.

q.q: In the 2005 study, experts found an average of four mistakes in a Wikipedia article and ____ in a Britannica article.
q.e: Paragraph 5 gives four and three mistakes.

q.q: Why is the coverage of Wikipedia uneven?
q.e: Paragraph 6 says the gaps reflect the interests of the volunteers.
o: A. Wikipedia has a plan to ignore some subjects for ever
B. It reflects the interests of the people who volunteer
C. Some subjects are banned
D. The Wikimedia Foundation selects the topics

q.q: In paragraph 6, "These gaps reflect the interests of the people who volunteer, not a deliberate plan." What does this mean?
q.e: The sentence says the unevenness is a natural result of volunteers' interests.
o: A. The gaps were created deliberately by the people who run the site, so that some subjects stay hidden
B. The gaps do not exist, because every subject is covered
C. The gaps exist because of what editors choose to write about, not because someone decided to leave things out
D. The gaps show that the volunteers are paid to choose their subjects, and they avoid the difficult ones

q.q: The writer states that Wikipedia has more articles than any other website.
q.e: The passage does not compare the number of articles with other websites.

q.q: What does the writer suggest about readers who use Wikipedia?
q.e: Paragraph 7 and 8 advise treating Wikipedia as a starting point and checking sources.
o: A. They should trust popular pages completely, since many people read them
B. They should only use small pages that few people edit
C. They should check the sources and not accept everything without question
D. They should avoid the internet and use only printed books

q.q: Which of the following best describes the writer's attitude to Wikipedia?
q.e: The writer praises how it works but discusses gaps and warns readers to check sources.
o: A. Strongly negative, since the writer sees nothing good in it
B. Balanced: appreciative of its achievements but aware of its limits
C. Completely uncritical, since the writer sees no problems in it
D. Uninterested, since the writer does not mind about it

q.q: Which of the following is the best summary of the whole passage?
q.e: The passage explains why it works, how accurate it is and why care is needed.
o: A. Wikipedia has been shown to be much less accurate than Britannica, and no student should ever read it
B. Wikipedia works through volunteers, rules and transparency, and is surprisingly accurate, but has gaps and should be used with care
C. Wikipedia is a perfect source and should replace books in all schools, since it never contains an error, and everyone can trust it.
D. Wikipedia is paid for by schools and governments, so its articles are always correct and need no check

ps.e: When Wikipedia was launched in January 2001, many people laughed at the idea.
ps.b: ২০০১ সালের জানুয়ারিতে যখন উইকিপিডিয়া চালু হয়, অনেক মানুষ এই ধারণা নিয়ে হেসেছিল।

ps.e: An encyclopedia that anyone in the world could edit, without a degree, a salary or an editor-in-chief?
ps.b: এমন একটি বিশ্বকোষ, যা পৃথিবীর যে কেউ সম্পাদনা করতে পারবে, ডিগ্রি, বেতন বা প্রধান সম্পাদক ছাড়াই?

ps.e: It sounded like a recipe for chaos.
ps.b: এটি শোনাচ্ছিল বিশৃঙ্খলার রেসিপির মতো।

ps.e: Yet more than twenty years later, Wikipedia is one of the most visited websites on Earth, with millions of articles in English alone and versions in over three hundred languages.
ps.b: তবু বিশ বছরেরও বেশি পরে উইকিপিডিয়া পৃথিবীর সবচেয়ে বেশি দেখা ওয়েবসাইটগুলোর একটি, শুধু ইংরেজিতেই লক্ষ লক্ষ নিবন্ধ নিয়ে এবং তিনশোরও বেশি ভাষায় সংস্করণ নিয়ে।

ps.e: How has it survived?
ps.b: এটি কীভাবে টিকে রইল?

ps.e: The first part of the answer is people.
ps.b: উত্তরের প্রথম অংশ হলো মানুষ।

ps.e: Wikipedia is written and maintained by volunteers, most of whom are unpaid.
ps.b: উইকিপিডিয়া লেখা ও রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ করেন স্বেচ্ছাসেবকরা, যাঁদের বেশিরভাগই বেতন পান না।

ps.e: They are supported by a non-profit organisation, the Wikimedia Foundation, which pays for servers and legal protection but does not decide what the articles say.
ps.b: তাঁদের সহায়তা করে একটি অলাভজনক সংস্থা, উইকিমিডিয়া ফাউন্ডেশন, যা সার্ভার ও আইনি সুরক্ষার খরচ জোগায় কিন্তু নিবন্ধে কী লেখা থাকবে তা ঠিক করে না।

ps.e: Because anyone may correct a mistake, a large crowd of readers works as a very large team of proof-readers.
ps.b: যেহেতু যে কেউ ভুল সংশোধন করতে পারেন, পাঠকদের একটি বিশাল ভিড় বিশাল এক প্রুফ-সংশোধক দল হিসেবে কাজ করে।

ps.e: The second part is rules.
ps.b: দ্বিতীয় অংশ হলো নিয়ম।

ps.e: Wikipedia has a small number of core principles that every editor is expected to follow.
ps.b: উইকিপিডিয়ার অল্প কয়েকটি মূল নীতি আছে, যা প্রতিটি সম্পাদকের মেনে চলার কথা।

ps.e: Articles must be written from a neutral point of view, which means that they should describe the main viewpoints fairly rather than argue for one.
ps.b: নিবন্ধ লিখতে হবে নিরপেক্ষ দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি থেকে, অর্থাৎ কোনো একটি পক্ষের হয়ে যুক্তি না দিয়ে প্রধান দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিগুলো ন্যায্যভাবে বর্ণনা করতে হবে।

ps.e: They must not contain "original research", so editors cannot publish their own theories.
ps.b: এতে "নিজস্ব গবেষণা" থাকা চলবে না, অর্থাৎ সম্পাদকরা নিজেদের তত্ত্ব প্রকাশ করতে পারেন না।

ps.e: And most importantly, claims must be verifiable: a reader should be able to check them in a reliable published source, such as a book, a journal or a respected newspaper.
ps.b: আর সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ, দাবিগুলো হতে হবে যাচাইযোগ্য: একজন পাঠক যেন বই, জার্নাল বা সম্মানিত সংবাদপত্রের মতো কোনো নির্ভরযোগ্য প্রকাশিত উৎসে তা মিলিয়ে দেখতে পারেন।

ps.e: This is why a well-edited article is full of numbered notes.
ps.b: এ কারণেই একটি ভালোভাবে সম্পাদিত নিবন্ধ নম্বর দেওয়া টীকায় ভরা থাকে।

ps.e: The third part is visibility.
ps.b: তৃতীয় অংশ হলো দৃশ্যমানতা।

ps.e: Every change made to an article is recorded, and anyone can look at the page history to see who changed what and when.
ps.b: একটি নিবন্ধে করা প্রতিটি পরিবর্তন নথিভুক্ত হয়, আর যে কেউ পাতার ইতিহাস দেখে বুঝতে পারেন কে কখন কী বদলেছে।

ps.e: Each article also has a talk page where editors discuss disagreements.
ps.b: প্রতিটি নিবন্ধের একটি আলোচনা পাতাও আছে, যেখানে সম্পাদকরা মতভেদ নিয়ে কথা বলেন।

ps.e: If someone adds nonsense, other editors can undo the change within minutes, and sometimes within seconds, with the help of automatic programs that detect obvious vandalism.
ps.b: কেউ আজেবাজে কিছু যোগ করলে অন্য সম্পাদকরা কয়েক মিনিটের মধ্যে, কখনও কয়েক সেকেন্ডে, পরিবর্তনটি বাতিল করতে পারেন, সুস্পষ্ট নষ্টামি শনাক্ত করা স্বয়ংক্রিয় প্রোগ্রামের সাহায্যে।

ps.e: Articles on controversial subjects can be "protected", so that only experienced editors are allowed to change them.
ps.b: বিতর্কিত বিষয়ের নিবন্ধ "সুরক্ষিত" করা যায়, যাতে কেবল অভিজ্ঞ সম্পাদকরাই সেগুলো পরিবর্তন করতে পারেন।

ps.e: But how accurate is Wikipedia?
ps.b: কিন্তু উইকিপিডিয়া কতটা নির্ভুল?

ps.e: In 2005, the journal Nature asked experts to compare forty-two scientific entries from Wikipedia with the same entries in the Encyclopaedia Britannica.
ps.b: ২০০৫ সালে নেচার জার্নাল বিশেষজ্ঞদের বলল উইকিপিডিয়ার বিয়াল্লিশটি বৈজ্ঞানিক নিবন্ধ এনসাইক্লোপিডিয়া ব্রিটানিকার একই নিবন্ধের সঙ্গে তুলনা করতে।

ps.e: The reviewers found that the two were close in accuracy: the experts found an average of four mistakes in a Wikipedia article and three in a Britannica article.
ps.b: পর্যালোচকরা দেখলেন দুটি প্রায় কাছাকাছি নির্ভুল: বিশেষজ্ঞরা উইকিপিডিয়ার একটি নিবন্ধে গড়ে চারটি ভুল এবং ব্রিটানিকার একটিতে তিনটি ভুল পেলেন।

ps.e: Britannica disputed the study, and the encyclopedias have changed greatly since then, but the result surprised many people.
ps.b: ব্রিটানিকা গবেষণাটি নিয়ে আপত্তি জানাল, আর তখন থেকে বিশ্বকোষগুলো অনেক বদলেছে, কিন্তু ফলাফলটি অনেককে অবাক করেছিল।

ps.e: This does not mean that Wikipedia is perfect.
ps.b: এর মানে এই নয় যে উইকিপিডিয়া নিখুঁত।

ps.e: Its coverage is uneven.
ps.b: এর আলোচনার পরিধি অসম।

ps.e: Subjects that interest its typical editors, such as computing, popular music and science fiction, are covered in great depth, while others receive far less attention.
ps.b: এর সাধারণ সম্পাদকদের আগ্রহের বিষয়, যেমন কম্পিউটিং, জনপ্রিয় সংগীত ও বিজ্ঞান-কল্পকাহিনি, গভীরভাবে আলোচিত, অন্যদিকে অন্য বিষয়গুলো অনেক কম মনোযোগ পায়।

ps.e: Surveys suggest that only a small minority of its editors are women, and that a much smaller share of its biographies are about women than about men.
ps.b: জরিপ ইঙ্গিত দেয় যে এর সম্পাদকদের মধ্যে নারী কেবল একটি ছোট সংখ্যালঘু, আর এর জীবনীগুলোর মধ্যে পুরুষদের তুলনায় নারীদের নিয়ে জীবনীর অংশ অনেক ছোট।

ps.e: Information about places and cultures outside Europe and North America can also be thin.
ps.b: ইউরোপ ও উত্তর আমেরিকার বাইরের স্থান ও সংস্কৃতি নিয়ে তথ্যও অপর্যাপ্ত হতে পারে।

ps.e: These gaps reflect the interests of the people who volunteer, not a deliberate plan.
ps.b: এই ফাঁকগুলো স্বেচ্ছাসেবকদের আগ্রহের প্রতিফলন, কোনো ইচ্ছাকৃত পরিকল্পনা নয়।

ps.e: There is a further problem: readers cannot always tell the difference between a well-checked article and one that has hardly been reviewed.
ps.b: আরও একটি সমস্যা আছে: পাঠকরা সবসময় বুঝতে পারেন না কোন নিবন্ধ ভালোভাবে যাচাই করা, আর কোনটি প্রায় পর্যালোচনাই হয়নি।

ps.e: A page about a popular topic may have been examined by hundreds of editors, while a page about a small village may have been written by one person years ago.
ps.b: জনপ্রিয় বিষয়ের একটি পাতা শত শত সম্পাদকের দৃষ্টিতে পড়ে থাকতে পারে, অন্যদিকে একটি ছোট গ্রামের পাতা হয়তো বহু বছর আগে একজন মানুষ লিখেছেন।

ps.e: Researchers therefore advise treating Wikipedia as a starting point rather than a final authority.
ps.b: তাই গবেষকরা উইকিপিডিয়াকে চূড়ান্ত প্রামাণিক উৎস না ভেবে শুরুর বিন্দু হিসেবে দেখার পরামর্শ দেন।

ps.e: Teachers often tell students not to cite Wikipedia in their essays, and the advice is sensible.
ps.b: শিক্ষকরা প্রায়ই শিক্ষার্থীদের বলেন প্রবন্ধে উইকিপিডিয়ার উদ্ধৃতি না দিতে, আর পরামর্শটি বুদ্ধিমানের।

ps.e: But many teachers also admit that it is a good place to begin.
ps.b: কিন্তু অনেক শিক্ষকই স্বীকার করেন যে শুরু করার জন্য এটি একটি ভালো জায়গা।

ps.e: The most valuable habit is to follow the links at the bottom of the page and read the original sources.
ps.b: সবচেয়ে মূল্যবান অভ্যাস হলো পাতার নিচের লিংকগুলো অনুসরণ করে মূল উৎস পড়া।

ps.e: Used in this way, Wikipedia shows what its founders hoped: that millions of strangers, working by shared rules, can build something useful.
ps.b: এভাবে ব্যবহার করলে উইকিপিডিয়া দেখায় এর প্রতিষ্ঠাতারা যা আশা করেছিলেন: লক্ষ লক্ষ অপরিচিত মানুষ, ভাগ করা নিয়মে কাজ করে, কিছু কাজের জিনিস গড়ে তুলতে পারে।

ps.e: It also shows that no source, however popular, should be believed without being questioned.
ps.b: এটি এও দেখায় যে কোনো উৎসকেই, যত জনপ্রিয়ই হোক, প্রশ্ন না করে বিশ্বাস করা উচিত নয়।

cmp/26.title: The Trees That Stand in the Sea
cmp/26.src: FAO; Global Mangrove Alliance; McIvor et al.; Mikoko Pamoja
p: A mangrove forest looks like a mistake. Trees stand with their roots in salty water, in mud that is flooded twice a day by the tide. Most plants would die in these conditions, because salt is poisonous to them and mud contains almost no oxygen. Mangroves, however, have learned to live in exactly this place, and by doing so they have become one of the most valuable ecosystems on the planet.

Their survival depends on clever adaptations. Many mangrove species can remove salt from the water they absorb, and some push it out through their leaves, where it can be seen as white crystals. To breathe in the oxygen-poor mud, the trees grow special roots that rise up out of the ground like small snorkels. Other roots arch down from the trunk like stilts, which hold the tree steady against waves. Together, this tangle of roots forms a living wall at the edge of the sea.

That wall is very useful to people. When waves and storm surges move through a mangrove forest, the roots and trunks slow the water down and take away its energy. Studies suggest that a belt of mangroves one hundred metres wide can reduce the height of waves by between about thirteen and sixty-six percent, depending on the density of the trees. For communities in places such as Bangladesh, which is regularly hit by cyclones, a healthy mangrove belt can mean the difference between a damaged village and a destroyed one.

Mangroves also feed and shelter wildlife. The submerged roots are a nursery for young fish, crabs and shrimps, which are protected from larger predators among the tangle. Many of these animals will later move out to open water and be caught by fishermen. The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, which stretches across Bangladesh and India, is also home to the Bengal tiger, one of the few tigers that regularly swims between islands.

There is a third benefit, which scientists have only recently understood. The thick, wet mud under mangroves stores huge amounts of carbon, because the dead leaves and roots break down very slowly without oxygen. Per hectare, mangroves can hold more carbon than most land forests. If a mangrove forest is cut down, much of this carbon may escape into the air as carbon dioxide, which adds to global warming.

Despite all this, mangroves have been disappearing. The world has lost about a fifth of its mangroves since 1980. Many were cleared to build shrimp farms, which can make quick money, and others were replaced by farmland, roads and hotels. For a long time people regarded mangroves as useless swamps, and only recently have they discovered how much they provide for free.

Some places are trying to reverse the damage. In Vietnam and Bangladesh, villagers and governments have planted mangroves along the coast for decades. In Bangladesh, the Forest Department has planted mangroves on new mud islands since the 1960s, and these young forests now help to shelter villages from cyclones. In Kenya, a project called Mikoko Pamoja, whose name means "mangroves together", pays local people to protect their forest, using money raised from selling carbon credits to companies that want to balance their emissions. The scheme also pays for school books and clean water.

Restoration is not simple. Mangroves planted in the wrong place, for example on mud flats that have never held trees, often die. Success depends on understanding how water flows and on involving local people. Still, the evidence is clear that mangroves are worth protecting. A tree that stands in the sea turns out to be one of the most useful friends that a coast can have.

q.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
q.e: The passage describes how mangroves survive, what they provide and how they are threatened.
o: A. To argue that people should not live near the sea, because it is dangerous
B. To describe how shrimp are farmed
C. To explain why mangroves are valuable and why they need protection
D. To compare mangroves with desert plants

q.q: Salt is harmful to most plants.
q.e: Paragraph 1 says salt is poisonous to most plants.

q.q: How do some mangroves get rid of salt?
q.e: Paragraph 2 says some push salt out through their leaves.
o: A. They store it in their roots
B. They wash it away with fresh water
C. They turn it into sugar
D. They push it out through their leaves

q.q: What is the purpose of the roots that rise up from the mud like snorkels?
q.e: Paragraph 2 says they are for breathing in oxygen-poor mud.
o: A. To catch fish
B. To hold the tree against waves
C. To store carbon
D. To help the trees breathe

q.q: Which sentence best sums up paragraph 3?
q.e: Paragraph 3 explains how roots take energy from waves and protect villages.
o: A. Mangroves increase the height of waves that reach the coast
B. Mangroves are damaged by cyclones, so they cannot protect anything
C. The roots of mangroves slow waves and can protect communities from storms
D. Waves cannot enter mangrove forests, because the water is too deep

q.q: A belt of mangroves one hundred metres wide can reduce the height of waves by between about thirteen and ____ percent.
q.e: Paragraph 3 gives a range of thirteen to sixty-six percent.

q.q: In paragraph 2, the word "adaptations" means:
q.e: Adaptations are features that help a plant or animal live in its environment.
o: A. different kinds of salt that are found in sea water near the mouth of rivers
B. changes in a living thing that help it to survive in its environment
C. types of food that animals eat in the forest during the wet season of the year
D. damaged roots that no longer take up water because of the salt in the mud

q.q: The Sundarbans lie only in Bangladesh.
q.e: Paragraph 4 says it stretches across Bangladesh and India.

q.q: Why are mangrove roots a good nursery for young fish?
q.e: Paragraph 4 says the tangle protects them from larger predators.
o: A. Young fish are protected from larger predators there
B. The water there is warmer than in the open sea
C. The roots give the young fish food every day
D. Fishermen cannot enter the thick forest of roots

q.q: Why do mangroves store so much carbon?
o: A. Dead leaves and roots break down very slowly in the mud without oxygen
B. They absorb carbon directly from the water of the sea into their leaves and roots
C. They are very tall and hold a great deal of wood
D. They grow faster than most other kinds of trees

q.q: About a fifth of the world's mangroves have been lost since 1980.
In paragraph 6, "people regarded mangroves as useless swamps, and only recently have they discovered how much they provide for free". What does this mean?
q.e: The sentence says that people once undervalued mangroves and have only recently seen their benefits.
o: A. People used to think mangroves had no value, but now understand that they give many benefits without cost
B. Mangroves were sold at low prices to people who cut them down and used the wood for building
C. Swamps are always useless, and cannot give any benefit to people who live near them
D. Mangroves were removed for free by the local government, which wanted the land for building

q.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 8 about restoring mangroves?
q.e: Paragraph 8 says that planting in the wrong place often fails and that success needs understanding and local involvement.
o: A. It should be left only to governments, and not to local people
B. It is not worth the effort, because the forests grow back alone
C. It is easy and always successful, wherever the trees are planted
D. It needs careful planning and cannot be done just by planting anywhere

q.q: What is the writer's attitude to mangroves?
q.e: The writer admires their value and is concerned about their loss.
o: A. Doubtful about their value to people
B. Admiring and concerned
C. Humorous about the way they grow
D. Indifferent to what happens to them

q.q: Which of the following is the best summary of the whole passage?
q.e: The passage covers the adaptations, the benefits, the losses and restoration.
o: A. Mangroves have no real value, so people can safely cut them down for farms and for building
B. Mangroves are useful only for shrimp farming and for making charcoal, so they should be cleared
C. Mangroves protect coasts, support wildlife and store carbon, but many have been lost, and careful restoration is needed
D. Mangroves are found only in Kenya, where they are protected by law, and no other country has any, so they cannot be saved.

q.q: Mangroves grow faster in cold water than in warm water.
q.e: The passage does not mention this.

ps.e: A mangrove forest looks like a mistake.
ps.b: একটি ম্যানগ্রোভ বন দেখতে ভুলের মতো লাগে।

ps.e: Trees stand with their roots in salty water, in mud that is flooded twice a day by the tide.
ps.b: গাছগুলো লবণাক্ত পানিতে মূল ডুবিয়ে দাঁড়িয়ে থাকে, এমন কাদায় যা দিনে দুবার জোয়ারে প্লাবিত হয়।

ps.e: Most plants would die in these conditions, because salt is poisonous to them and mud contains almost no oxygen.
ps.b: বেশিরভাগ উদ্ভিদ এমন পরিস্থিতিতে মরে যেত, কারণ লবণ তাদের জন্য বিষাক্ত আর কাদায় অক্সিজেন প্রায় থাকেই না।

ps.e: Mangroves, however, have learned to live in exactly this place, and by doing so they have become one of the most valuable ecosystems on the planet.
ps.b: কিন্তু ম্যানগ্রোভ ঠিক এই জায়গায় বাঁচতে শিখেছে, আর তা করে গ্রহের সবচেয়ে মূল্যবান বাস্তুতন্ত্রগুলোর একটিতে পরিণত হয়েছে।

ps.e: Their survival depends on clever adaptations.
ps.b: এদের টিকে থাকা নির্ভর করে চতুর অভিযোজনের ওপর।

ps.e: Many mangrove species can remove salt from the water they absorb, and some push it out through their leaves, where it can be seen as white crystals.
ps.b: অনেক ম্যানগ্রোভ প্রজাতি যে পানি শোষণ করে তা থেকে লবণ বের করে দিতে পারে, আর কিছু প্রজাতি পাতার মধ্য দিয়ে তা বাইরে ঠেলে দেয়, যেখানে তা সাদা স্ফটিক হিসেবে দেখা যায়।

ps.e: To breathe in the oxygen-poor mud, the trees grow special roots that rise up out of the ground like small snorkels.
ps.b: অক্সিজেন-স্বল্প কাদায় শ্বাস নিতে গাছগুলো এমন বিশেষ মূল জন্মায় যা ছোট শ্বাসনলের মতো মাটি ফুঁড়ে ওপরে ওঠে।

ps.e: Other roots arch down from the trunk like stilts, which hold the tree steady against waves.
ps.b: অন্য মূলগুলো কাণ্ড থেকে খুঁটির মতো বাঁকা হয়ে নিচে নামে, যা ঢেউয়ের মুখে গাছকে স্থির রাখে।

ps.e: Together, this tangle of roots forms a living wall at the edge of the sea.
ps.b: সব মিলিয়ে, এই মূলের জট সমুদ্রের কিনারায় একটি জীবন্ত দেয়াল তৈরি করে।

ps.e: That wall is very useful to people.
ps.b: এই দেয়াল মানুষের জন্য খুবই কাজের।

ps.e: When waves and storm surges move through a mangrove forest, the roots and trunks slow the water down and take away its energy.
ps.b: ঢেউ ও ঝড়ের জলোচ্ছ্বাস যখন ম্যানগ্রোভ বনের মধ্য দিয়ে যায়, মূল ও কাণ্ড পানির গতি কমিয়ে তার শক্তি কেড়ে নেয়।

ps.e: Studies suggest that a belt of mangroves one hundred metres wide can reduce the height of waves by between about thirteen and sixty-six percent, depending on the density of the trees.
ps.b: গবেষণা ইঙ্গিত দেয়, একশ মিটার চওড়া ম্যানগ্রোভের বেষ্টনী গাছের ঘনত্ব অনুযায়ী ঢেউয়ের উচ্চতা প্রায় তেরো থেকে ছেষট্টি শতাংশ পর্যন্ত কমাতে পারে।

ps.e: For communities in places such as Bangladesh, which is regularly hit by cyclones, a healthy mangrove belt can mean the difference between a damaged village and a destroyed one.
ps.b: বাংলাদেশের মতো জায়গার জনগোষ্ঠীর জন্য, যেখানে নিয়মিত ঘূর্ণিঝড় আঘাত হানে, সুস্থ ম্যানগ্রোভ বেষ্টনী একটি ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত গ্রাম আর একটি ধ্বংস হয়ে যাওয়া গ্রামের মধ্যে পার্থক্য গড়ে দিতে পারে।

ps.e: Mangroves also feed and shelter wildlife.
ps.b: ম্যানগ্রোভ বন্যপ্রাণীকে খাদ্য ও আশ্রয়ও দেয়।

ps.e: The submerged roots are a nursery for young fish, crabs and shrimps, which are protected from larger predators among the tangle.
ps.b: পানিতে ডোবা মূলগুলো তরুণ মাছ, কাঁকড়া ও চিংড়ির জন্য শিশুশালা, যারা জটের ভেতরে বড় শিকারিদের হাত থেকে সুরক্ষিত থাকে।

ps.e: Many of these animals will later move out to open water and be caught by fishermen.
ps.b: এই প্রাণীগুলোর অনেকে পরে খোলা পানিতে চলে যায় এবং জেলেদের জালে ধরা পড়ে।

ps.e: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, which stretches across Bangladesh and India, is also home to the Bengal tiger, one of the few tigers that regularly swims between islands.
ps.b: সুন্দরবন, বিশ্বের বৃহত্তম ম্যানগ্রোভ বন, যা বাংলাদেশ ও ভারত জুড়ে বিস্তৃত, বেঙ্গল টাইগারেরও আবাস, যা এমন কয়েকটি বাঘের একটি যারা নিয়মিত দ্বীপ থেকে দ্বীপে সাঁতার কাটে।

ps.e: There is a third benefit, which scientists have only recently understood.
ps.b: এর একটি তৃতীয় উপকারিতা আছে, যা বিজ্ঞানীরা সম্প্রতি বুঝতে শুরু করেছেন।

ps.e: The thick, wet mud under mangroves stores huge amounts of carbon, because the dead leaves and roots break down very slowly without oxygen.
ps.b: ম্যানগ্রোভের নিচের পুরু, ভেজা কাদা প্রচুর কার্বন জমা রাখে, কারণ অক্সিজেন ছাড়া মরা পাতা ও মূল খুব ধীরে ধীরে পচে।

ps.e: Per hectare, mangroves can hold more carbon than most land forests.
ps.b: প্রতি হেক্টরে ম্যানগ্রোভ স্থলের বেশিরভাগ বনের চেয়ে বেশি কার্বন ধরে রাখতে পারে।

ps.e: If a mangrove forest is cut down, much of this carbon may escape into the air as carbon dioxide, which adds to global warming.
ps.b: কোনো ম্যানগ্রোভ বন কেটে ফেললে এই কার্বনের অনেকটাই কার্বন ডাইঅক্সাইড হয়ে বাতাসে মিশে যেতে পারে, যা বৈশ্বিক উষ্ণায়নে ভূমিকা রাখে।

ps.e: Despite all this, mangroves have been disappearing.
ps.b: এত কিছুর পরও ম্যানগ্রোভ হারিয়ে যাচ্ছে।

ps.e: The world has lost about a fifth of its mangroves since 1980.
ps.b: ১৯৮০ সাল থেকে বিশ্ব তার ম্যানগ্রোভের প্রায় এক-পঞ্চমাংশ হারিয়েছে।

ps.e: Many were cleared to build shrimp farms, which can make quick money, and others were replaced by farmland, roads and hotels.
ps.b: অনেক বন সাফ করা হয়েছে চিংড়ি খামার বানাতে, যা দ্রুত টাকা আনে, আর অন্যগুলোর জায়গায় এসেছে কৃষিজমি, সড়ক ও হোটেল।

ps.e: For a long time people regarded mangroves as useless swamps, and only recently have they discovered how much they provide for free.
ps.b: দীর্ঘদিন মানুষ ম্যানগ্রোভকে অকেজো জলাভূমি মনে করত, আর সম্প্রতি তারা আবিষ্কার করেছে এরা বিনামূল্যে কতটা কিছু দেয়।

ps.e: Some places are trying to reverse the damage.
ps.b: কিছু জায়গা ক্ষতি উল্টে দেওয়ার চেষ্টা করছে।

ps.e: In Vietnam and Bangladesh, villagers and governments have planted mangroves along the coast for decades.
ps.b: ভিয়েতনাম ও বাংলাদেশে গ্রামবাসী ও সরকার কয়েক দশক ধরে উপকূল বরাবর ম্যানগ্রোভ রোপণ করে আসছে।

ps.e: In Bangladesh, the Forest Department has planted mangroves on new mud islands since the 1960s, and these young forests now help to shelter villages from cyclones.
ps.b: বাংলাদেশে বন বিভাগ ১৯৬০-এর দশক থেকে নতুন জেগে ওঠা কাদার চরে ম্যানগ্রোভ লাগিয়েছে, আর এই তরুণ বনগুলো এখন ঘূর্ণিঝড় থেকে গ্রামগুলোকে আড়াল করতে সাহায্য করে।

ps.e: In Kenya, a project called Mikoko Pamoja, whose name means "mangroves together", pays local people to protect their forest, using money raised from selling carbon credits to companies that want to balance their emissions.
ps.b: কেনিয়ায় মিকোকো পামোজা নামের একটি প্রকল্প, যার নামের অর্থ "ম্যানগ্রোভ একসঙ্গে", স্থানীয় মানুষকে তাদের বন রক্ষার জন্য টাকা দেয়, এই টাকা আসে কার্বন ক্রেডিট বিক্রি থেকে, যা কিনে সেইসব কোম্পানি যারা তাদের নির্গমন ভারসাম্যে আনতে চায়।

ps.e: The scheme also pays for school books and clean water.
ps.b: প্রকল্পটি স্কুলের বই ও পরিষ্কার পানির খরচও জোগায়।

ps.e: Restoration is not simple.
ps.b: পুনরুদ্ধার সহজ নয়।

ps.e: Mangroves planted in the wrong place, for example on mud flats that have never held trees, often die.
ps.b: ভুল জায়গায় লাগানো ম্যানগ্রোভ, যেমন কাদার চরে যেখানে কখনও গাছ ছিল না, প্রায়ই মরে যায়।

ps.e: Success depends on understanding how water flows and on involving local people.
ps.b: সাফল্য নির্ভর করে পানি কীভাবে বইছে তা বোঝার ওপর এবং স্থানীয় মানুষকে যুক্ত করার ওপর।

ps.e: Still, the evidence is clear that mangroves are worth protecting.
ps.b: তবুও প্রমাণ স্পষ্ট যে ম্যানগ্রোভ রক্ষার যোগ্য।

ps.e: A tree that stands in the sea turns out to be one of the most useful friends that a coast can have.
ps.b: সমুদ্রে দাঁড়িয়ে থাকা একটি গাছ শেষ পর্যন্ত একটি উপকূলের সবচেয়ে কাজের বন্ধুদের একজন হয়ে ওঠে।

cmp/27.sub: How long it really takes to form a habit
cmp/27.title: Do Habits Really Take Twenty-One Days?
cmp/27.src: Lally et al.; Wood, Quinn and Kashy; Wood and Neal; Maltz; Gollwitzer
p: Almost everyone has heard that it takes twenty-one days to form a new habit. Magazines repeat it, motivational speakers say it with confidence, and many people start a new routine, such as exercising or learning a language, with a three-week plan in mind. When day twenty-two arrives and the habit still feels like hard work, they often decide that they are failing. The truth is more reassuring, and rather more interesting.

The twenty-one-day idea seems to come from the 1960s, when a plastic surgeon named Maxwell Maltz noticed that his patients needed about three weeks to get used to their new faces. He wrote that it takes "a minimum of about 21 days" for an old mental image to fade. Over the years, the words "a minimum of about" were forgotten, and an observation about patients became a rule about everyone's habits.

A more careful study was carried out in 2009 by Phillippa Lally and her colleagues at University College London. They asked ninety-six volunteers to choose a simple behaviour, such as drinking a glass of water at lunch or going for a short run before dinner, and to do it every day for twelve weeks. Each evening, the volunteers recorded how automatic the behaviour felt, meaning how much they did it without thinking.

The results were striking. On average, it took sixty-six days for the behaviour to reach its peak automaticity. But the average hides a huge range: for some people and some habits, it took as few as eighteen days, while for others it took more than two hundred and fifty. Simple actions, such as drinking water, became automatic faster than demanding ones, such as doing fifty sit-ups.

The same study contained some good news. Missing a single day did not seem to harm the process in a significant way. The volunteers who forgot once or twice quickly returned to their earlier progress. The lesson is that habits are not destroyed by one slip, so the all-or-nothing thinking that leads people to give up after a missed day is not justified.

Why do habits matter so much? Researchers estimate that a large share of what we do every day, perhaps around forty percent, is done more or less automatically, in the same place and at the same time, often while we are thinking about something else. A habit saves mental effort. Once a behaviour is linked to a regular situation, such as brushing your teeth after breakfast, the situation itself triggers the action, and you no longer have to rely on willpower.

This suggests a practical way to build a new habit: connect it to something you already do. Psychologists call this an implementation intention, and it takes the form "When X happens, I will do Y". A person who says "After I pour my morning coffee, I will write for ten minutes" is more likely to succeed than a person who simply says "I will write more", because the coffee becomes a reminder. It also helps to begin with an action that is so small that it is almost impossible to skip.

None of this makes habit-building easy, and no number of days guarantees success. Different people, goals and environments produce very different timelines. Still, the research is encouraging for those who have struggled. If a new routine feels difficult after three weeks, that is normal, not a sign of weakness. It is wiser to be patient, to start small and to expect that the process may take two months or more.

q.q: What is the main point of the passage?
q.e: The passage shows that research found a wide range, with an average of sixty-six days.
o: A. Habits take different amounts of time to form, and the twenty-one-day rule is a myth
B. Habits are formed only by famous people with strong willpower, and ordinary people cannot make them
C. Everyone can form a habit in twenty-one days if they try hard enough and never miss a day
D. Habits can never be changed once they have been formed, even if a person tries very hard

q.q: According to paragraph 2, how did the twenty-one-day idea begin?
q.e: Paragraph 2 says Maxwell Maltz noticed that patients needed about three weeks to adjust.
o: A. From a government study of many people and their habits
B. From a magazine competition about the best advice
C. From the observation of a plastic surgeon about his patients
D. From a school experiment carried out in the last century

q.q: What did Maltz actually write, according to paragraph 2?
q.e: Paragraph 2 quotes "a minimum of about 21 days".
o: A. That habits cannot be formed by people over a certain age
B. That it takes a minimum of about 21 days for an old mental image to fade
C. That habits last for 21 years once they have been formed
D. That all habits take exactly 21 days to form for every person who tries

q.q: The study by Lally and colleagues involved ninety-six volunteers.
The volunteers recorded how automatic a behaviour felt every morning.
q.e: Paragraph 3 says they recorded it each evening.

q.q: On average, it took ____ days for the behaviour to reach its peak automaticity.
q.e: Paragraph 4 gives the average as sixty-six days.

q.q: Which sentence best sums up paragraph 4?
q.e: Paragraph 4 gives the average and the wide range.
o: A. Habit formation takes an average of sixty-six days, but varies greatly
B. All habits take the same amount of time to form in every person.
C. Complex habits are faster to form than simple ones.
D. Nobody formed a habit in the study, so the results were unclear.

q.q: Habits formed faster when the action was simple.
q.e: Paragraph 4 says simple actions became automatic faster than demanding ones.

q.q: What did the study find about missing a day?
q.e: Paragraph 5 says missing one day did not seem to harm the process significantly.
o: A. Missing a day destroyed the habit
B. Missing a day made the habit stronger and easier to keep
C. Nobody missed a day
D. One missed day did not seriously harm progress

q.q: In paragraph 5, "the all-or-nothing thinking that leads people to give up after a missed day is not justified". What does this mean?
q.e: The sentence says that quitting after one slip is not supported by the evidence.
o: A. People should never miss a day if they want to build a habit
B. Giving up is the best option when a day has been missed
C. There is no good reason to quit just because you missed one day
D. Missing a day always ruins all the progress that has been made

q.q: In paragraph 6, the word "triggers" is closest in meaning to:
q.e: Here, a situation triggers an action, meaning it starts it.
o: A. hide or cover from other people
B. measure or count carefully
C. stop or prevent from starting
D. start or cause

q.q: The writer states that implementation intentions are used only by athletes.
q.e: The passage does not say who uses implementation intentions.

q.q: What does the writer suggest about a habit that still feels difficult after three weeks?
q.e: Paragraph 8 says it is normal and not a sign of weakness.
o: A. The habit is dangerous
B. This is normal and does not mean failure
C. The person is not suited to the habit
D. The person should give up

q.q: What is the writer's attitude towards the twenty-one-day rule?
q.e: The writer questions the rule but offers encouragement.
o: A. Uninterested in the research on habits
B. Sceptical but encouraging to readers
C. Fully convinced that it is true for every habit
D. Angry with the people who first invented it

q.q: Which of the following is the best summary of the whole passage?
q.e: The passage covers the origin of the myth, the study results and practical advice.
o: A. The twenty-one-day rule is a myth; research shows habits can take much longer and vary, and starting small with a clear cue helps
B. Habits are impossible to build, whatever people do, and all the research shows that they soon fail
C. Habits depend only on willpower, and not on cues or small steps, according to the research that is described in the passage, and they form quickly.
D. Habits form in a single day if the cue is clear, and research shows that no one needs to wait longer

g.demanding: কঠিন, বেশি পরিশ্রম দাবি করে এমন
g.implementation intention: কাজ শুরুর আগেই ঠিক করা পরিকল্পনা

ps.e: Almost everyone has heard that it takes twenty-one days to form a new habit.
ps.b: প্রায় সবাই শুনেছেন যে নতুন অভ্যাস গড়তে একুশ দিন লাগে।

ps.e: Magazines repeat it, motivational speakers say it with confidence, and many people start a new routine, such as exercising or learning a language, with a three-week plan in mind.
ps.b: ম্যাগাজিনগুলো এটি আওড়ায়, অনুপ্রেরণামূলক বক্তারা আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে এটি বলেন, আর অনেক মানুষ ব্যায়াম বা ভাষা শেখার মতো নতুন রুটিন শুরু করেন তিন সপ্তাহের পরিকল্পনা মাথায় রেখে।

ps.e: When day twenty-two arrives and the habit still feels like hard work, they often decide that they are failing.
ps.b: বাইশতম দিন এলে যখন অভ্যাসটি তখনও কঠিন পরিশ্রম মনে হয়, তারা প্রায়ই ভাবেন তারা ব্যর্থ হচ্ছেন।

ps.e: The truth is more reassuring, and rather more interesting.
ps.b: সত্যটি আরও আশ্বাসদায়ক, এবং কিছুটা বেশি মজার।

ps.e: The twenty-one-day idea seems to come from the 1960s, when a plastic surgeon named Maxwell Maltz noticed that his patients needed about three weeks to get used to their new faces.
ps.b: একুশ দিনের ধারণাটি মনে হয় এসেছে ১৯৬০-এর দশক থেকে, যখন ম্যাক্সওয়েল ম্যাল্টজ নামের একজন প্লাস্টিক সার্জন লক্ষ করেন যে তাঁর রোগীদের নতুন মুখের সঙ্গে অভ্যস্ত হতে প্রায় তিন সপ্তাহ লাগে।

ps.e: He wrote that it takes "a minimum of about 21 days" for an old mental image to fade.
ps.b: তিনি লিখেছিলেন, মনের পুরোনো ছবি ফিকে হতে "ন্যূনতম প্রায় ২১ দিন" লাগে।

ps.e: Over the years, the words "a minimum of about" were forgotten, and an observation about patients became a rule about everyone's habits.
ps.b: বছরের পর বছর ধরে "ন্যূনতম প্রায়" শব্দগুলো ভুলে যাওয়া হলো, আর রোগীদের নিয়ে একটি পর্যবেক্ষণ সবার অভ্যাস নিয়ে একটি নিয়মে পরিণত হলো।

ps.e: A more careful study was carried out in 2009 by Phillippa Lally and her colleagues at University College London.
ps.b: ২০০৯ সালে ইউনিভার্সিটি কলেজ লন্ডনে ফিলিপ্পা ল্যালি ও তাঁর সহকর্মীরা আরও সতর্ক একটি গবেষণা চালান।

ps.e: They asked ninety-six volunteers to choose a simple behaviour, such as drinking a glass of water at lunch or going for a short run before dinner, and to do it every day for twelve weeks.
ps.b: তাঁরা ছিয়ানব্বইজন স্বেচ্ছাসেবককে একটি সহজ আচরণ বেছে নিতে বললেন, যেমন দুপুরের খাবারের সময় এক গ্লাস পানি পান করা বা রাতের খাবারের আগে ছোট দৌড় দেওয়া, এবং তা বারো সপ্তাহ ধরে প্রতিদিন করতে বললেন।

ps.e: Each evening, the volunteers recorded how automatic the behaviour felt, meaning how much they did it without thinking.
ps.b: প্রতি সন্ধ্যায় স্বেচ্ছাসেবকরা লিখে রাখতেন আচরণটি কতটা স্বয়ংক্রিয় মনে হচ্ছে, অর্থাৎ না ভেবেই তারা কতটা তা করছেন।

ps.e: The results were striking.
ps.b: ফলাফল ছিল চমকপ্রদ।

ps.e: On average, it took sixty-six days for the behaviour to reach its peak automaticity.
ps.b: গড়ে আচরণটির স্বয়ংক্রিয়তার সর্বোচ্চ মাত্রায় পৌঁছাতে ছেষট্টি দিন লেগেছিল।

ps.e: But the average hides a huge range: for some people and some habits, it took as few as eighteen days, while for others it took more than two hundred and fifty.
ps.b: কিন্তু গড়টি বিশাল একটি পরিসর আড়াল করে: কিছু মানুষ ও কিছু অভ্যাসের জন্য মাত্র আঠারো দিন লেগেছিল, আবার অন্যদের জন্য লেগেছিল দুই শ পঞ্চাশেরও বেশি।

ps.e: Simple actions, such as drinking water, became automatic faster than demanding ones, such as doing fifty sit-ups.
ps.b: পানি পান করার মতো সহজ কাজ পঞ্চাশটি সিট-আপ করার মতো কঠিন কাজের চেয়ে দ্রুত স্বয়ংক্রিয় হয়ে গিয়েছিল।

ps.e: The same study contained some good news.
ps.b: একই গবেষণায় কিছু ভালো খবরও ছিল।

ps.e: Missing a single day did not seem to harm the process in a significant way.
ps.b: একটি দিন বাদ পড়ায় প্রক্রিয়াটির উল্লেখযোগ্য ক্ষতি হয়েছে বলে মনে হয়নি।

ps.e: The volunteers who forgot once or twice quickly returned to their earlier progress.
ps.b: যারা একবার-দুবার ভুলে গিয়েছিলেন, তাঁরা দ্রুত আগের অগ্রগতিতে ফিরে এসেছিলেন।

ps.e: The lesson is that habits are not destroyed by one slip, so the all-or-nothing thinking that leads people to give up after a missed day is not justified.
ps.b: শিক্ষা হলো, একটি ছোট ভুলে অভ্যাস নষ্ট হয় না, তাই একটি দিন বাদ পড়লেই হাল ছেড়ে দেওয়ার যে "সব নয়তো কিছু নয়" চিন্তা, তার কোনো যুক্তি নেই।

ps.e: Why do habits matter so much?
ps.b: অভ্যাস এত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কেন?

ps.e: Researchers estimate that a large share of what we do every day, perhaps around forty percent, is done more or less automatically, in the same place and at the same time, often while we are thinking about something else.
ps.b: গবেষকরা অনুমান করেন, আমরা প্রতিদিন যা করি তার একটি বড় অংশ, হয়তো প্রায় চল্লিশ শতাংশ, কমবেশি স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে করা হয়, একই জায়গায় ও একই সময়ে, প্রায়ই অন্য কিছু ভাবতে ভাবতে।

ps.e: A habit saves mental effort.
ps.b: অভ্যাস মানসিক পরিশ্রম বাঁচায়।

ps.e: Once a behaviour is linked to a regular situation, such as brushing your teeth after breakfast, the situation itself triggers the action, and you no longer have to rely on willpower.
ps.b: কোনো আচরণ একবার একটি নিয়মিত পরিস্থিতির সঙ্গে যুক্ত হয়ে গেলে, যেমন সকালের নাশতার পর দাঁত ব্রাশ করা, পরিস্থিতিটিই কাজটি শুরু করিয়ে দেয়, আর তখন ইচ্ছাশক্তির ওপর নির্ভর করতে হয় না।

ps.e: This suggests a practical way to build a new habit: connect it to something you already do.
ps.b: এটি নতুন অভ্যাস গড়ার একটি বাস্তব উপায় নির্দেশ করে: এটিকে এমন কিছুর সঙ্গে যুক্ত করুন যা আপনি আগে থেকেই করেন।

ps.e: Psychologists call this an implementation intention, and it takes the form "When X happens, I will do Y".
ps.b: মনোবিজ্ঞানীরা একে বলেন ইমপ্লিমেন্টেশন ইনটেনশন, যার রূপ হলো "যখন X ঘটবে, আমি Y করব"।

ps.e: A person who says "After I pour my morning coffee, I will write for ten minutes" is more likely to succeed than a person who simply says "I will write more", because the coffee becomes a reminder.
ps.b: যিনি বলেন "সকালের কফি ঢালার পর আমি দশ মিনিট লিখব", তিনি সফল হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা বেশি রাখেন তার চেয়ে যিনি কেবল বলেন "আমি আরও লিখব", কারণ কফিটি তখন একটি স্মারক হয়ে ওঠে।

ps.e: It also helps to begin with an action that is so small that it is almost impossible to skip.
ps.b: এমন কাজ দিয়ে শুরু করাও সাহায্য করে যা এত ছোট যে বাদ দেওয়া প্রায় অসম্ভব।

ps.e: None of this makes habit-building easy, and no number of days guarantees success.
ps.b: এর কিছুই অভ্যাস গড়াকে সহজ করে না, আর কোনো দিনসংখ্যাই সাফল্যের নিশ্চয়তা দেয় না।

ps.e: Different people, goals and environments produce very different timelines.
ps.b: ভিন্ন মানুষ, লক্ষ্য ও পরিবেশ ভিন্ন ভিন্ন সময়সীমা তৈরি করে।

ps.e: Still, the research is encouraging for those who have struggled.
ps.b: তবু যারা সংগ্রাম করেছেন তাঁদের জন্য গবেষণা উৎসাহজনক।

ps.e: If a new routine feels difficult after three weeks, that is normal, not a sign of weakness.
ps.b: তিন সপ্তাহ পরও একটি নতুন রুটিন কঠিন লাগলে তা স্বাভাবিক, দুর্বলতার লক্ষণ নয়।

ps.e: It is wiser to be patient, to start small and to expect that the process may take two months or more.
ps.b: ধৈর্য ধরা, ছোট থেকে শুরু করা এবং আশা করা বুদ্ধিমানের যে প্রক্রিয়াটিতে দুই মাস বা তার বেশি লাগতে পারে।

cmp/28.title: The Day the Railways Changed the Clock
cmp/28.src: Royal Museums Greenwich; Library of Congress; Smithsonian; International Meridian Conference
p: Imagine that you are travelling by train across a country, and that every town you pass has a different time. In one town it is noon, in the next it is five minutes past, and in the third it is ten minutes past. This was not a joke or a story. It was daily life in many countries before the middle of the nineteenth century, and the solution came not from a scientist's laboratory but from the railways.

For most of history, time was a local matter. Each town set its clocks by the sun, so that noon was the moment when the sun was at its highest point in the sky. Because the Earth turns, the sun reaches this point later in places to the west. In Britain, for example, Bristol's noon came about ten minutes after London's. Nobody noticed or cared, because a journey on a horse or a boat was so slow that the difference seemed unimportant.

The railways changed this. Trains were fast, and they ran to a timetable. If every station along a line used a different local time, the timetable became a puzzle and accidents became possible. In 1840, the Great Western Railway in England decided to run all its trains by London time, which was the first step towards a single national time. By the late 1840s, most British railways used the same time, which people called "railway time".

The problem was bigger in North America, where the distances were much greater. By the 1880s, the railway companies of the United States and Canada used dozens of different local times, and passengers needed to study a confusing chart to plan a journey. On 18 November 1883, the railways introduced five standard time zones across the continent. Many towns adopted the new system on that day, which some newspapers described as "the day of two noons", because clocks were moved forward or back to match the new zones.

The new system was not welcomed by everyone. Some people were unhappy that their local time had been changed by private companies, and a few towns refused to follow it for years. But the advantages were obvious, and in 1918 the United States government made standard time the law.

The next step was global. In 1884, delegates from twenty-five countries met in Washington to agree on a common starting point for measuring longitude, which is the position of a place east or west on the Earth. They chose the line passing through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich in London, and it became the Prime Meridian. The world was then divided into twenty-four zones, each about fifteen degrees wide, so that the time in each zone is one hour different from its neighbour.

This tidy plan did not remove all the arguments. Many countries chose to follow their own political needs rather than the lines on the map. China, which is as wide as five time zones, has used a single time, Beijing time, since 1949, so in the far west of the country, in winter, the sun may not rise until around ten o'clock in the morning. India uses one time for the whole country, and its time is five and a half hours ahead of Greenwich, an unusual half-hour difference. Nepal is even more unusual, with a difference of five hours and forty-five minutes.

Today our phones change time automatically, and we rarely think about what lies behind the numbers on the screen. Yet every clock reminds us of a basic fact: time zones are an agreement, not a law of nature. They were invented when speed made local differences a problem, and they continue to be adjusted when politics and convenience demand it.

q.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
q.e: The passage traces how railways led to national and global standard time.
o: A. The Sun moves around the Earth, so time differs in each place
B. China has a single time zone, although it is a very large country
C. Clocks were first invented in the nineteenth century by railway workers, and they spread to every town
D. The railways created the need for standard time and led to the system of time zones

q.q: Before the nineteenth century, how did towns set their clocks?
q.e: Paragraph 2 says each town set its clocks by the sun.
o: A. By railway timetables that were printed in each town
B. By telegraph signals
C. By a national law
D. By the position of the sun

q.q: In Britain, Bristol's noon came about ten minutes before London's.
q.e: Paragraph 2 says Bristol's noon came about ten minutes after London's.

q.q: According to paragraph 3, why did the railways need a common time?
q.e: Paragraph 3 explains that different local times made the timetable a puzzle.
o: A. Trains were fast and ran to a timetable
B. Trains could not travel at night, and so they needed a clock
C. Passengers disliked clocks
D. The sun was unreliable

q.q: The Great Western Railway adopted London time in 1840.
Which sentence best sums up paragraph 4?
q.e: Paragraph 4 describes the confusion and the introduction of five zones.
o: A. Passengers liked the confusing chart of railway times, and asked the companies to keep it.
B. Railways in Canada refused to change their old clock times, and kept them until the year 1900.
C. North American railways introduced standard time zones in 1883 to solve a confusing situation
D. The United States had only one time for the whole country, which made the railways simple to run.

q.q: In 1883, the railways introduced five standard time zones across the ____.
All American towns accepted standard time immediately.
q.e: Paragraph 5 says a few towns refused to follow it for years.

q.q: What did the delegates in Washington choose in 1884?
q.e: Paragraph 6 says they chose the line through Greenwich.
o: A. The line passing through Paris, the capital of France
B. The line passing through Greenwich as the Prime Meridian
C. The line passing through Beijing, the capital of China
D. The line passing through New York, in the United States

q.q: In paragraph 7, "Many countries chose to follow their own political needs rather than the lines on the map." What does this mean?
q.e: The sentence says that political choices overrode the neat zones.
o: A. Countries ignored the idea of time and had no clocks until the end of the century
B. Countries redrew the map of the world to fit the zones, and changed their borders
C. Countries banned clocks, since people did not need them when the Sun was in the sky
D. Countries set their time according to what suited them, not strictly according to the zones

q.q: Why might the sun rise at around ten o'clock in the far west of China?
q.e: Paragraph 7 explains that China uses one time across a very wide country.
o: A. Because the sun is weaker
B. Because of daylight saving
C. Because the whole country uses Beijing time
D. Because the country is very cold in the north, so the days are short

q.q: The writer states that daylight saving time was invented in 1916.
q.e: The passage does not mention daylight saving time.

q.q: What is the writer's view of time zones in the last paragraph?
q.e: The writer says time zones are an agreement, not a law of nature.
o: A. They are a law of nature that nobody can change
B. They are a human agreement that can be changed
C. They are a mistake that should be corrected at once
D. They are no longer needed, since computers give the time

q.q: Which of the following is the best summary of the whole passage?
q.e: The passage covers the origin, the railway solution, the global system and the exceptions.
o: A. Time zones began with railways and were organised globally in 1884, though countries still adjust them for their own reasons
B. Time zones were created by the Sun, and have never been changed by any country since they began, so every country follows them.
C. Time zones began in China, and then spread to Europe along the old trade routes by camel
D. Time zones are the same in every country of the world, and no country has ever adjusted them

ps.e: Imagine that you are travelling by train across a country, and that every town you pass has a different time.
ps.b: কল্পনা করুন, আপনি ট্রেনে একটি দেশ পাড়ি দিচ্ছেন, আর আপনি যে শহরেই পৌঁছান তার সময় আলাদা।

ps.e: In one town it is noon, in the next it is five minutes past, and in the third it is ten minutes past.
ps.b: একটি শহরে দুপুর বারোটা, পরেরটিতে বারোটা পাঁচ, আর তৃতীয়টিতে বারোটা দশ।

ps.e: This was not a joke or a story.
ps.b: এটি কোনো রসিকতা বা গল্প ছিল না।
